key_insight: RiVER shows that LLMs can be improved on coding tasks without ground-truth answers by learning from calibrated, score-based execution feedback.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical RL training recipe for algorithmic and code-generation systems where exact labels are unavailable but deterministic performance signals exist.
method: Uses ranking-induced verifiable rewards from execution scores instead of ground-truth solutions.
Applies reward calibration to reduce scale dominance across instances and frequency dominance from repeated weak samples.
Emphasizes top-ranked valid solutions while keeping bounded feedback for other correct candidates.
evidence_signal: Trained on 12 AtCoder Heuristic Contest tasks, RiVER improved ALE rating rank by 8.9% for Qwen3-8B and 9.4% for GLM-Z1-9B-0414, and also boosted exact-solution benchmarks by 2.4% on LiveCodeBench and 3.5% on USACO.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable deterministic execution feedback; noisy or poorly normalized scores could weaken the calibrated reward signal.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
